lesson.title: 3.10 Her hair is long
lesson.unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
lesson.unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
lesson.goal: Describe people with her/his + hair or eyes (Her hair is long. / His eyes are green.), next to A1+ 1.1's has (She has long hair.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.10 My, Your, His, and Her: A1 puts my, your, his and her before a name or a thing (his phone); A1+ 3.10 uses his and her to describe people. The one new grammar relationship is possessive + hair or eyes + be + a description (Her hair is long. / His eyes are green.), taught against A1+ 1.1's has + a description + noun (She has long hair. / He has green eyes.); eyes takes are. Three new close portraits show short and long hair and blue, green and brown eyes; A1+ 1.1's photos of Ana (long hair) and Luis (short hair) come back. A bank never sets one long-haired woman against another.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 3.10 his and her; A1 7.1 eyes; A1 2.8 and 2.13 blue, green, brown; A1+ 1.1 long and short hair and has; A1+ 3.3 she's.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say hair with no h-drop and eyes as one syllable (aiz); keep his and her short. Do not require native-like speed.
